FN-RU0KMY-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 269
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 05/03/2023
Senate Bill 269 as introduced creates the Alabama K-12 Capital Grant Program to provide to
eligible public K-12 entities grants, in amounts not to exceed $5 million per grant, to assist with:
(1) capital projects, (2) the payment of existing debt service, (3) correcting deferred maintenance
of existing facilities, (4) improving school security and safety, and (5) the provision of
technology and equipment for schools to expand educational opportunities. This bill creates the
K-12 Capital Grant Program Fund, into which the Legislature may appropriate funds
presumably from the Education Trust Fund, to facilitate the program. This bill also provides that
any unencumbered and unexpended balances remaining at the end of any fiscal year shall remain
in the Fund and used for the program until expended.
Additionally, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of: (1) the Office of
Lieutenant Governor to administer the program pursuant to the provisions of this bill; and (2)
the Examiners of Public Accounts to ensure compliance of the grant recipients with the
provisions of this bill.

FN-RU0KMY-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 269
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Arthur Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 05/22/2023
Senate Bill 269 as passed the Senate would create the non-reverting K-12 Capital Grant
Program Fund in the State Treasury, into which the Legislature may appropriate funds, to
facilitate the Alabama K-12 Capital Grant Program, created by this bill and administered by the
Office of Lieutenant Governor, to fund grants to eligible public K-12 entities, in amounts not to
exceed $5 million per grant, for: (1) capital projects; (2) the payment of existing debt service;
(3) deferred maintenance of existing facilities; (4) improving school security and safety; and (5)
the provision of technology and equipment for schools to expand educational opportunities.
Further, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of the Office of Lieutenant
Governor to administer the program, pursuant to the provisions of this bill, which could be
offset, in whole or in part, by the utilization of up to 0.25% of the available funding for the
administration of the program.
This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of the Department of the Examiners
of Public Accounts to examine compliance of the grant recipients with the provisions of this
bill.
